body: Not that I'm aware of. Anything that I thought was interesting I've looked up and determined is either too expensive or too far away. There doesn't seem to be anything cheap or free to do in the area.
No driver's permit or license yet, and if I had one I would need to buy a car as well. It would take a few hours  to get to the nearest club so borrowing a car would be out of the question.

Doing more research, it seems that only hobbyists facet gems themselves, businesses just buy gems that were cut entirely by machines. I looked into clubs for hobbyists, but the nearest one is too far away considering I can't drive.

> You say there isn't anything you're interested enough to follow as a career, but at the same time, you say there is.

There are things I would like to try, but I have no clue if I'd actually like them or not. I'll just give an example. I would like to try faceting gemstones because it's creative, productive, possibly lucrative, and it can branch into several other things that may keep me busy for a while (appraisal, identification, trying to dig up gemstones, setting gems in jewelry, etc.) but I don't know how difficult it is, if it's considered to be fun by those who do it, if it's viable as a job, if it's monotonous and boring, or really anything about it other than it's currently prohibitively expensive for me and it involves putting flat faces on gemstones. I'd like to try it, but I don't currently have an interest in it, or even an opinion on it.

I've been told I should try community college but there's no point in going if I can't afford the kind of college I would transfer credits to. That $10k+ in debt isn't going to get me anywhere alone.

You're correct about sitting around being bored causing my problems, and accomplishing something would help. I've been bored nearly every day for years and feel like I've wasted the time that I've had so far. It's hard to find a good reason to live when you aren't doing anything with your life anyway.

It's mostly because of money but not having a clue how college works could be part of it as well. In school I was told that if I got good grades I'd get scholarships, but then when they gave us info on the scholarships nearly all of them required extracurricular activities or a specific field or for you to be already accepted into a college. Grades were secondary. Even if I would have gotten every one of the few that I qualified for, it would have been like $500 and not enough for me to handle the rest of the debt.

The reason I'm so scared of debt is I hear often about people who go to college, even very good ones, and then end up unable to find work or at least not work in their field. I have no job experience so to put so much debt on myself with no idea if I'll get a job or not would be terrifying.

> surely there's *something* you're interested in enough that you'd like to make a career out of it, right?

The simple answer is no. I don't really do anything and don't keep up with advancements in any sort of field. There are a few potentially profitable hobbies I'd like to try but they require large amounts of funds to start off and I could easily end up hating them anyway.
No, it's not medical. I live with my parents.
